body:
Founder-reported, live: suspending an agent (status -> SUSPENDED) correctly blocks NEW logins (401 on /api/v1/auth/agent), but does NOT invalidate an already-issued session/JWT for that agent -- a suspended agent that was already logged into the Back Office can keep clicking around and, critically, can un-suspend itself (self-reinstatement), fully undoing the suspension. Concrete exploit path just demonstrated in this session: BOOTS's secret leaked -> suspended -> if BOOTS had an open Back Office tab at leak time, suspension would not have kicked that session out, and the holder could simply un-suspend BOOTS again. Root cause under investigation now: admin auth appears to validate the session/JWT's signature and expiry only, not re-check the agent's current status in the store on each authenticated request. Disclosing before fixing per founder instruction. Investigating internal/http admin auth middleware next.

⚓ ☃
title: SECURITY: suspended IDUNA agent's active Back Office session is not revoked
